Class 5 · Chapter 10 of 10

Codes, reflections and logic puzzles

Test every clue and distinguish turning, mirroring and flipping.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Charts, averages and true statements. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can use codes, series and ranking clues.
  • I can follow directions and count combinations.
  • I can reason about mirror clocks and reflected words.
  • I can order words by their logical meaning and find an exact embedded figure.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Letter series

Look at each part of the pair separately.

In DZ, EY, FX, GW the first letters move forward and the second letters move back.

The next pair is HV.

Screen 2 of 5

Mirror images

A mirror at the side flips left and right.

The order of the letters turns around, and each letter is flipped.

Test it with a small mirror at home.

Screen 3 of 5

Count the combinations

7 flag colours and 6 flag symbols make 7 × 6 = 42 combinations.

Each colour pairs with every symbol.

An array shows the pairs in rows and columns.

Screen 4 of 5

Turns and directions

A rover faces east, moves forward 2, turns left and moves forward 2.

Left from east is north.

Draw the path before you decide where it ends.

Screen 5 of 5

Mirror clocks

At 1:30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 1 and 2.

The angle between them is 135 degrees.

Check every hand, not only the minute hand.

Words to know
series
A list of letters or numbers that follows a rule.
mirror image
The flipped copy you see in a mirror.
combination
One choice from each group put together.

For parents

What your child learns

A Venn diagram shows groups that may overlap. If 35 pupils and 5 play neither, then 30 play at least one. Music and chess overlap by 19 + 17 − 30 = 6, so only music is 13.

A common slip

Children often count the overlap twice. Find the overlap first, then take it from each group. Check that all parts add to the total.

5-minute home activity: Two circles

  1. Draw two overlapping circles on paper.
  2. Ask family which they like among two choices.
  3. Put each name in the right part.
  4. Check that every part adds to the total.
